title: ARC: workload arc-based batching recommendation + safe apply runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build and run ARC (Adaptive Recommendation Core) — a workload-arc-driven batching recommendation engine that synthesizes lightweight workload profiles, heuristic selectors, and a continuous parameter feedback loop. ARC will produce safe batch/cache configs, run shadow evaluations, and provide automated staged apply/rollback with metric-based abort conditions.
acceptance_criteria: ARC produces per-customer recommended batch and KV-cache policies with clear rationale, stored as immutable profiles
Automated shadow evaluation (1–7 days) compares baseline vs recommended and reports token-cost delta, p50/p95 latency, and accuracy regression for configured prompt sets
Safe apply rollout: canary (1%), ramp (5%, 25%, 100%) with automatic rollback if cost or latency exceeds thresholds
No more than 5% p95 latency regression for any canary traffic slice; token cost reduction >= 8% on at least 60% of evaluated workloads
Operator UI shows diff, rollback button, and exact metrics that triggered aborts
Integration tests for config apply/rollback, telemetry triggers, and feature-flagged rollout path
Documentation (runbook + run experiment template) available and linked in PR
steps: Finalize workload-arc definition: time-window, session-affinity, distribution buckets (short/medium/long), and cold-start heuristics
Implement profiler: lightweight sampler that captures sequence length, token distribution, KV cache hit-rate proxy, and burstiness score
Design heuristic selector mapping arcs -> candidate batch sizes, max microbatch latency, KV-cache TTL suggestions, and throttling knobs
Build shadow evaluation runner: run candidate config in parallel (no impact) for X% sampled traffic and aggregate metrics to dashboard
Create safety policy engine: thresholds, statistical tests (Welch/Bootstrap), and hysteresis rules for noisy signals
Implement staged apply controller: canary/ramp/abort/rollback flow, feature-flag gating, and operator override
Add observability: per-profile cost delta, latency percentiles, accuracy regressions, and alert/annotation hooks in Console
Write end-to-end tests and staging rollout plan; run 2 pilot customers under NDA
comments: 2025-01-11: Kickoff meeting — aligned on profiling schema and data retention. Action: Aisha to draft profiler spec (confluence).
2025-01-22: Decision to keep profiler lightweight (sample at 0.5% by default) to avoid telemetry cost blowup. Marco to prototype sampling agent in runtime sidecar.
2025-01-28: UX sync — Console team will add a 'Recommended Changes' diff card; dependency on PM-88 for card design.
2025-02-04: Shadow runner PoC metrics look promising: sample workload saw projected 12% token cost saving with <2% p95 regression in internal staging.
2025-02-12: Added safety hysteresis: require 48 hours of stable improvement before ramping beyond 25%.
2025-02-14: Security review flag set to false after infra review; will re-evaluate for enterprise deployments with KMS workflows.
notes: We intentionally scope ARC as recommendation + safe-apply pipeline rather than full autonomous control for first release.
Heuristics will be tunable via an operator-facing policy file; aim for sensible defaults to reduce operator cognitive load.
Workload arcs map: short chat (<128 tokens), medium completion (128–1024), long context (>1024) — different batch heuristics for each.
Accuracy regression checks use our existing eval harness; teams must register a prompt-set per customer to enable regression detection.
